test_title: PYST 51: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 19 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following best defines the concentration of a solution?

options.text: The amount of solute present in a given amount of solution
The amount of solution present in a given amount of solute
The amount of solvent present in a given amount of solution
The amount of solvent present in a given amount of solute

solution:
The correct answer is __**The amount of solute present in a given amount of solution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **concentration** of a solution refers to the **amount of solute** dissolved in a particular **amount (mass or volume)** of the **solution** or **solvent**.
 
• It is a quantitative measure that helps determine how "strong" or "weak" a solution is based on the proportion of its components.
 
• **Statement 1**: This statement correctly defines concentration as the ratio of the **solute** to the total **solution**. This is the standard way to express concentration in chemistry. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 2**: This statement suggests that concentration is the amount of solution in a solute, which is logically incorrect as the **solute** is a component of the **solution**, not vice versa. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 3**: This statement describes the amount of **solvent** in a solution; while this indicates the degree of **dilution**, the term "concentration" specifically tracks the **solute**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 4**: This statement defines the amount of solvent in a given amount of solute, which is essentially the inverse of the solubility relationship and does not represent the definition of concentration. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Common mathematical expressions for concentration include **Mass by mass percentage**, **Mass by volume percentage**, and **Molarity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Solute and Solvent:**

 
 
• The **Solute** is the substance that is **dissolved** in another substance (usually present in a **smaller quantity**), such as **salt** or **sugar**.
 
• The **Solvent** is the substance in which the solute is dissolved (usually present in a **larger quantity**), such as **water** or **alcohol**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Solutions based on Concentration:**
 
 
• **Dilute Solution**: A solution containing a very **small amount of solute** relative to the amount of solvent.
 
• **Concentrated Solution**: A solution containing a **large amount of solute** dissolved in the solvent.
 
• **Saturated Solution**: A solution in which **no more solute** can be dissolved at a specific **temperature**.
 
• **Unsaturated Solution**: A solution where the amount of solute is **less than** the **saturation level**, meaning more can still be dissolved.
 
 
 
• **Solubility:**
 
 
• The **maximum amount of solute** that can be dissolved in **100 grams** of solvent at a specific **temperature** is known as its **solubility**.
 
• Factors such as **temperature** and **pressure** can significantly affect the solubility of solids and gases in liquids.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mass by Mass Percentage of a solution**: Calculated as (**Mass of solute** / **Mass of solution**) × **100**.
 
• **Mass by Volume Percentage of a solution**: Calculated as (**Mass of solute** / **Volume of solution**) × **100**.
 
• **Molarity (M)**: It is defined as the **number of moles of solute** dissolved in **1 liter** of solution. It is the most commonly used unit of concentration in laboratories.
 
• **Molality (m)**: It is defined as the **moles of solute** per **kilogram of solvent**. Unlike molarity, molality does not change with **temperature** changes because mass is constant.
 
• **Parts Per Million (ppm)**: Used for expressing very **low concentrations**, such as the amount of **pollutants** in the **atmosphere** or **water**.
